coordinate_space: B16 unapproved 2400x1200 planar drawing; periodic x wrapping by 2400, distance in drawing units only; NO kilometers or meters.

geometry_methods.angle: Per vertex, angle between incoming/outgoing vectors from B16 coordinates (0..180 degrees). Acute if under 30; it may be legitimate tip, not necessarily defect.
geometry_methods.intersection: Strict proper non-neighbor segments crossing via opposite 2D orientation sign products. Touching endpoints, collinear overlaps and topology repairs not separately solved.
geometry_methods.paired_boundary_distance: Shortest Euclidean segment-to-segment distance across distinct polygon boundaries, with source x periodic copies -2400,0,+2400. Spatial hash expanded by 12 drawing units to enumerate possible pairs. Gives drawing gap index only.
geometry_methods.nearby_same_polygon_boundaries: For potential narrow-neck screening, compare segments with cyclic vertex-step separation >= max(10, floor(0.06 * polygon_vertex_count)). Many close results on finely sampled smooth loops are NOT verified land bridges.
geometry_methods.containment: Test one vertex of each polygon against the other polygon even through ±2400 x periodic copies; absence of contained test points is not rigorous polygon overlap proof if polygons cross.
limitations: A segment crossing detector limited to proper intersections is not sufficient to rule out all touching/collinear nonmanifold geometry.
No reliable narrow land bridge is confirmed; nonlocal within-polygon proximity is only an exploratory geometry signal.
Near coast pair does not imply a land bridge or a navigable strait. Width at map coordinates cannot be converted to km.
Many B16 polygons contain numerous closely spaced vertices (e.g. 88/400) as a deliberate aesthetic coast treatment; smoothing indiscriminately would destroy source detail.
Do not automatically repair acute tips, close sea gaps, delete islands, shift approved countries or replace original B16 polygons.
Map is candidate noncanonical geography; no official global continent latitudes, geologic mechanism or local names assigned.
